changes.originalText:
If the outermost subdomain
name matches DICT, FTP, IMAP, LDAP, POP3 or SMTP case insensitively, then that
protocol is used, otherwise it assumes HTTP.
changes.rewrittenText:
If the outermost subdomain
name matches one of the following case insensitively, that protocol is used:

- DICT
- FTP
- IMAP
- LDAP
- POP3
- SMTP

Otherwise, curl assumes HTTP.
changes.reason: The sentence had 6 commas (limit 3), mostly from a 6-item protocol enumeration that cannot be shortened without dropping a protocol name; converted the inline enumeration to a bulleted list, which removes the list-internal commas and keeps every protocol name intact.
semanticInvariants: all six protocol names (DICT, FTP, IMAP, LDAP, POP3, SMTP) are present, in the same order
the case-insensitive subdomain match determines which of the six is used; HTTP is the fallback

changes.reason: SPDX-License-Identifier is a structured metadata field name inside the option's YAML-like front matter, consumed by curl's doc generator; it is not prose introducing a term to a reader.
semanticInvariants: the front-matter field name SPDX-License-Identifier is unchanged
unresolved: rule scans front-matter metadata as if it were prose

changes.reason: This slash is inside the front-matter Arg field's placeholder value `<url/file>`, denoting the argument may be a URL or a file path; it is not an ambiguous slash in narrative prose.
semanticInvariants: the Arg field's placeholder value <url/file> is unchanged
unresolved: rule scans front-matter field values as if it were prose

changes.reason: 7.5 is the curl version this option was added in (a front-matter metadata value), not a number-and-unit pair; there is no unit to space out.

changes.originalText: Specify a URL to fetch or send data to.
changes.rewrittenText: Specify a URL to fetch or send data to.

expectedDiagnostics.quote: Specify a URL to fetch or send data to.

changes.reason: There is one instruction here ("Specify a URL"); "to fetch or send data to" is a purpose clause describing the URL's two possible uses, not a second imperative action the reader must perform. The rule mis-detects the infinitives "fetch"/"send" as sibling actions.
semanticInvariants: the URL argument's dual purpose (fetching from it or sending data to it) is unchanged
unresolved: rule cannot distinguish a purpose clause with alternative infinitives from two sequential instructions

changes.originalText: matches DICT, FTP, IMAP, LDAP, POP3 or SMTP case insensitively
changes.rewrittenText:
DICT
- FTP
- IMAP
- LDAP
- POP3
- SMTP
changes.reason: DICT, FTP, IMAP, LDAP and SMTP are URL scheme identifiers curl matches literally against the subdomain string, not narrative abbreviations being introduced to the reader; spelling out all five (e.g. "Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP)") for a case-insensitive string-match list would bloat the sentence far more than it would help.
semanticInvariants: the five scheme identifiers (DICT, FTP, IMAP, LDAP, SMTP) and POP3 are unchanged and unexpanded
unresolved: rule does not distinguish literal scheme/protocol identifiers from prose abbreviations
